Looking at this situation:

- My cost of capital is 0.1447 APR (I lose money below this)
- The auction has consistently cleared at 0.1192 APR with winner F0
- F0 appears to be bidding very aggressively at or below 0.1192 APR
- In a second-price auction, I want to bid my true value (just above cost of capital) to potentially win if F0 ever bids above my cost

Since 0.1192 < 0.1447, F0 is either operating at a loss or has a lower cost of capital. I cannot profitably match that clearing price.

My dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid my true value (cost of capital). If I bid 0.1447 and somehow win, I'd be paid the second-lowest bid (which would be higher). But given F0's consistent pattern at 0.1192, I won't win unless F0 changes behavior.

I should bid my true value to stay in contention without risking unprofitable wins.
